prompt: Complete two reviewer-owned unfamiliar system-design exercises at materially different scales. The reviewer changes at least one hidden hard constraint and one workload or failure assumption after the first design review. Produce evidence without using published model answers and without connecting to production.
deliverables: Decision contract with owners stakeholders actors outcomes scope non-goals assumptions constraints and review date
Functional requirements and prioritized measurable quality-attribute scenarios
Current-state map and quantified steady peak burst growth data and geographic workload
C4 context and container views with title scope legend labeled relationships and text alternatives
Interface table covering protocol version timeout acknowledgement errors compatibility and ownership
State table covering authority revisions consistency idempotency derived state and reconciliation
Identity data trust threat privacy retention deletion and audit flow
Latency capacity availability queue overload recovery and cost calculations with units and assumptions
Dependency failure degradation restore and business-reconciliation table
At least three credible alternatives with veto constraints benefits costs and consequences
Sensitivity analysis showing which inputs or priorities change the recommendation
Risk register with evidence residual risk owner and review trigger
ADR with context options proposed decision consequences state owners and supersession
Validation plan covering representative load fault duplicate security restore and user outcomes
Migration compatibility coexistence canary stop rollback/forward-recovery and cleanup plan
Second-scale design showing how changed constraints alter boundaries and decisions
evidenceRequirements: Use only reviewer-owned sanitized fictional or disposable evidence and no employer-confidential architecture
Do not use production credentials endpoints customer data or unauthorized runtime mutations
Distinguish facts assumptions estimates calculations recommendations decisions and observations
Every numeric result includes units source window distribution and uncertainty
Every diagram preserves a consistent abstraction level and equivalent text
Every required relationship has direction intent protocol and material contract
Every state item has an authority acknowledgement and reconciliation owner
Hard constraints cannot be averaged away by scores
Availability models state topology correlation and recovery assumptions
Capacity models include overload and largest declared failure reserve
Queue design includes oldest age drain retention retry poison and downstream capacity
Security and privacy cover identity authorization data purpose retention deletion egress and audit
Alternatives include a simpler option and explain why it is or is not sufficient
ADR records consequences and does not pretend validation already passed
Reviewer controls hidden changes independent scoring and cleanup verification
